## The three answers

**1. Hybrid — DIY the reps, buy one session.** His profile is
textbook adolescent over-arousal, not a dangerous-dog case, so the daily work is genuinely DIY-able. But
diagnosis (frustration vs. fear) and threshold-finding need an expert eye once, and working a
dog over threshold is *the* reason DIY reactivity training fails. One $350 session now beats a $2,400 package later.

Recommended spend ~$650–740 all-in.

**2. Four local

options, real prices** — and one is time-sensitive:

| Option | Price | Notes |
|---|---|

---|
| HSSV Top Dogs Level 1 | **$300** | 6 wks online, **starts Tue 19 Aug,

6:15pm** — evening, purpose-built for leash reactivity |
| Good Sit (Mountain View) | **$350** | 90-min

one-off in-home + free consult; force-free |
| Lynn Brown, CPDT-KA | call |

408-218-8332; best credential/specialty match, no published rate |
| D For Dogz | $2,400 / $4,200 | 2–6x

benchmark; skip unless escalating |

**3. Four-week plan** — week 1 foundations and management only (zero reactivity work), week 2 Engage-Disengage
Level 1, week 3 Level 2 plus closing distance 1–5 steps at a time, week 4 integration ending in an explicit escal

ate-or-continue decision.

## Things worth flagging

I put a **red-flag self-check first**, before any spending — seven items (
bite history, can't hold him, redirects onto you, can't take food at any distance, aggressive off-leash too). If any is true, the DIY plan is the wrong answer and you should bu

y a package instead. Five minutes that could save six wasted weeks.

I also added
a **trigger log with a baseline measurement** to the prep, because otherwise "it feels a bit better" is your only week-4 data — not enough to decide on a $2,400 purch
ase. And a **border collie enrichment track**: this breed is bred to be triggered by movement, and an under-stimulated collie is a more reactive one

, so some of this may be an unmet-needs problem in a training problem's clothing.

**Two things I couldn't determine remotely**
, both now prep tasks: whether he's a frustrated greeter or fearful (the test is off
-leash behaviour — don't do it at a dog park), and his actual threshold distance. Both change the plan's p

ace and both are the first things to tell a trainer.

site warns they may be slow to reply — text, don't email. D For Dogz lists no Saturday and a 7pm we

ekday cutoff, which may not fit you.
